## Manual Overview

This manual provides the information needed to participate in {{< var project.name >}}. The manual is divided into five sections ([General information](#sec-generalinfo), [Getting Started](#sec-gettingstarted), [Setting up the experiment](#sec-setup), [Running the experiment](#sec-running) & [After data collection](#sec-aftercollection)). Each section is divided into chapters, which you can jump to using the navigation panel on the left of the screen.

<br>

## {{< var project.name >}} Overview

{{< var project.number >}} is a cross-lab effort to provide an empirical basis for discussions of replicability as well as cultural, developmental, and methodological variability in infant perception/cognition research. In this project, we are examining drivers of infants’ familiarity vs. novelty preference through a collaboratively-designed “best test” of a popular model of infants’ visual preference for familiar and novel stimuli [@hunter1988]. More details about the background, design and hypotheses can be found in the {{< var link.stage1rr >}} [@kosie]. In the following sections, we provide instructions for getting ready to run the experiment, implementing the experiment in your lab, and reporting data back to the project as a whole. Thanks for joining us!

![Hunter and Ames model of infant attention (adapted from Bergmann and Cristia, 2016)](images/HunterAmesFig.png){#fig-hunterames}
